correctness.rationale: For n>=3 and 0<a,b, a!=b, Fourier eigenvalues of the biased ring generator have imaginary parts (a-b)sin(2pi k/n). The real circulant exponential P(t) is symmetric iff every sampling phase lies in pi Z. For n>=5 both sin(2pi/n),sin(4pi/n) are nonzero; their rational ratio forces 2cos(2pi/n) a rational algebraic integer, hence integer; 0<2cos<2 forces n=6. Direct sine sets for n=3,4,6 give precisely t=2m pi/(sqrt3|a-b|) for 3,6 and m pi/|a-b| for 4. At even m phases all +1 so P=e^{tQsym}; at odd m the first nontrivial Fourier eigenvalue is strictly negative, excluding an exponential of a reversible continuous-time generator. Sampled KL entropy zero iff P symmetric since P(t)>0. Independently computed numerical matrix exponentials and Fourier eigenvalues for the three resonant sizes (m=1,2), tested negative modes and even-m symmetric exponentials; exact algebraic-integer proof covers all n.
